STALENESS AUDIT (2026-09-14, read-only; nothing in the engine changed).

Prior runs and the versions they measured:
- R01–R04 resume bench: 0.1 to 0.5, Jul 8–11.
- S2-R01: 0.9.2. S2-R02: 0.10.0.
- Drift scenarios 3 and 4: 0.25.1, pricing and smoke runs only.
- Driver 4.1 proof: pre-release code, before the two driver bugs b065fc5 fixed for 0.30.0.
- Micro-perf pins: Jul 20 – Aug 8.
No run covers 0.31.0.

Claims with no current backing:
- "<2% drift": no graded run exists (scenario 3 had n=2 packets; scenario 4 stopped at task 4.1).
- "2.44M vs 5.80M billed tokens per task": one run against one hand-picked manual session.

Fixed per-session overhead, measured on the session-driver record by building 0.10.0 / 0.25.1 / 0.31.0 in the scratchpad:
- SessionStart digest: 6,129 / 8,574 / 8,574 bytes.
- MCP tool definitions: 7 / 10 / 12 tools, 4,130 / 9,728 / 14,179 characters (about 1.0k to 3.5k tokens, sent every turn).
- Protocol block that `sofar init` writes: 3,406 / 4,384 / 5,723 bytes.
- Total: about 2.5k tokens at 0.10.0, now about 5.6k, plus about 1.4k for the protocol block.
- Hook medians got FASTER (stop 55 → 24 ms). session-start is back up to 74 ms, likely the 0.26 shipping-notice git read (unconfirmed).
- Consequence: S2-R02's −32.1% cost result is the most stale; drift-certification is moderately stale; driver 4.1 is least stale.

PROPOSED BENCHMARK AREAS
- A0 Overhead footprint (deterministic, no model cost): digest bytes, tool-schema characters, protocol-block bytes, and hook/fold latency at 10 / 100 / 1000 initiatives. Pin it per release.
- A1 Cost: billed tokens per COMPLETED task, split into input, cache-write, cache-read and output, plus API-priced $. Plot it against task index to show the cost curve's shape.
- A2 Time: wall-clock per task; time and turns to the first productive edit (orientation latency); operator minutes and number of interventions.
- A3 Outcome: objective pass (tests and acceptance criteria) before grader scores; pass@1 plus pass^k consistency across k reps.
- A4 Continuity: re-explanation cost (M1), clarifying questions asked, recall probe (task 7; R02 W2 arm S was UNRECOVERABLE), and whether the session picks the correct next action.
- A5 Decision adherence: walked-into rate on rejected approaches and standing constraints (the <2% claim).
- A6 Grounding: fabricated paths, ids and decisions (R02: L 30% / S 21%).
- A7 Long-horizon degradation: quality and cost vs task index, and compaction events, for one long session vs fresh sessions.
- A8 Autonomy (`sofar drive`): tasks per run with no intervention, stall rate, needs_user precision, handoff-reason accuracy, recovery.
- A9 Portability: the same record and workload run through claude-code, codex and opencode.
- A10 Concurrency and integrity: parallel sessions, write-back collisions, zero log corruption.

BASELINES TO COMPARE AGAINST
- B0 Bare agent with no memory.
- B1 Agent plus a hand-maintained CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md and a notes file (the realistic default).
- B2 One long session with auto-compaction (arm L).
- B3 Third-party memory/task layers, e.g. Cline Memory Bank, claude-mem, Beads, Task Master. Verify that each still exists before selecting it.

Existing benchmarks such as SWE-bench and Terminal-Bench score single-session task success. None scores cross-session continuity. So A3 is table stakes, and A4 through A8 are where sofar's claim lives.

Machinery to reuse from handoff-bench (session-strategy-bench rejected building a new bench): pre-registration, byte-identical workloads W1/W2 (W3 never run), equalized arms (the planned R03 fix for the skills asymmetry), graders A/B/C, the fabricated-path sidecar, and cell isolation from drift-certification.

- A one-command reproducible harness.

- Fresh, uncontaminated tasks.

- Codex under a ChatGPT subscription: % of its limit.

Limits are not published in tokens, so each plan's own usage meter is calibrated before and after a quiet calibration run, and tokens per task come from transcripts.

(B) CURSOR ARM. Cursor.app is installed; the `cursor-agent` headless CLI is NOT.

These are read, never emitted, so this is not telemetry. Snapshots are compared release over release.

COMBINED IMPROVEMENT PLAN (2026-09-15). Synthesis of three research reports: SOTA memory/context engineering, self-improving systems, and a code root-cause pass over 7 smoke/calib cells. PREDICTED gains are written here BEFORE building (D10) and are checked in round 2. All figures are estimates.

CORRECTIONS to earlier claims:
- "Digest doubled 10k→20.7k" was a measurement error. 20.7k was the whole transcript line, with the digest stored twice and JSON-escaped. Real SessionStart output: S1 0 chars (no initiative yet, so nothing injected), S2 6,422 (calib-1) and 5,282 (smoke-4). No truncation.
- But STATUS_CHAR_LIMIT = 10_000 (projections/templates/status.ts:35) equals Claude Code's 10k hook cap, so there is zero headroom.
- S1's extra cost comes from TURNS, not prompt size. Claude sofar S1 made 39 API calls / 61 tool uses vs bare 18/34. The fixed prompt differs by only +1.4k tokens.

WAVE 1: correctness and quick wins (XS–S effort, on a branch during round 1)
- W1.1 Empty-repo SessionStart prints the Session id plus "no initiative yet: sofar new <slug> --goal, then plan" (event.ts:375-398). PREDICT: Claude S1 −3 to −4 turns (~250k cache-read), no split sessions.
- W1.2 Session registration race: lock or make idempotent (event.ts:713-715; Cursor fires hooks in parallel). PREDICT: duplicate session_started = 0 across round-2 cursor cells.
- W1.3 CLI payload reference `sofar event types`, plan/phase/goal lines in the AGENTS block, "one initiative per project/roadmap", accept any --source (envelope.ts:17 SOURCES has no cursor). PREDICT: Codex S1 −13 tool calls (~1M cache-read); Cursor and Codex create a project initiative WITH a plan in ≥2/3 reps.
- W1.4 Formatter defence: doctor check/fix for Biome (plus Prettier and markdownlint hazards); write .mcp.json Biome-friendly (init.ts:1118). PREDICT: agents editing biome.json or reformatting .mcp.json 3/7 → 0.
- W1.5 stdin/file input for `remember` and `event --payload`, a quoted-heredoc example, `remember --supersedes`. PREDICT: shell-mangling corrections → 0.
- W1.6 Drive diagnostics: carry the stderr tail/failure into the stall note (drive.ts:776, adapter exit record). PREDICT: every launch failure names its cause.

WAVE 2: bookkeeping and context (S–M)
- W2.1 Show the next D/M ids in the digest; drop the standing-constraint echo from update_task responses; batch task updates into end_session; server instructions to load core tools in ONE ToolSearch. PREDICT: sofar bookkeeping share of tool calls 32–38% → ≤20%; −3 to −5 turns per session.
- W2.2 Deduplicate the digest (rejected approaches repeat decision `over` text; constraints repeat rules), index-first and ≤6k chars with details fetched on demand (Claude auto-memory / OpenAI AGENTS-as-TOC pattern). PREDICT: S2+ digest −25% chars with no C2/C3 loss.
- W2.3 Cache-stable layout: static prefix first, no volatile counts at the top, changing reminders late via UserPromptSubmit (Manus/Anthropic caching). PREDICT: cache-creation tokens per session −15%.
- W2.4 Tool surface: trim descriptions (the `initiative` description repeats in ~10 tools) and move review/close/find to CLI-first. PREDICT: schemas 14.8k → ≤8k chars. Small cost lever: schemas are ~4% of S1.
- W2.5 Automatic capture through hooks (write-behind): commits with task-id prefix, test pass/fail, files, errors recorded deterministically from PostToolUse/Stop; the model logs only WHY. PREDICT: sofar MCP/CLI calls per session −40%. Unverified technique, so it needs its own arm.

WAVE 3: new capabilities (M)
- W3.1 Verification-gated drive: run the task's acceptance command before accepting task_done; failures go into the next handoff (LangChain harness-only +13.7 pts on Terminal-Bench). PREDICT: drive final pass rate +5 pts over round-1 drive.
- W3.2 Decision counters and supersession/valid_until (ACE itemised counters; Zep temporal validity) so stale decisions leave the digest without a model. PREDICT: C3 re-violation rate no worse at −10% digest.
- W3.3 Relevant-lessons injection: BM25/keyword match of rejected approaches and past failures at UserPromptSubmit, no model. PREDICT: C3 +5 pts.

WAVE 4: self-improvement (novel)
- L1 zero-model local adaptation. First capture outcomes: exit codes and is_error in post-tool, register PostToolUseFailure, count MCP rejects locally. That needs a schema Decision first (packages/schema/src), plus a Decision that local stats are NOT telemetry (never emitted, gitignored). Then `sofar tune --dry-run` mines events.jsonl. Its precision test: does it rediscover this loss study's rows (duplicate starts, corrections, bookkeeping share, lint friction)? Changes are proposed, not applied, and are reversible events.
- L2 `sofar improve`: the operator's own agent via `sofar drive` patches one ranked loss per initiative, with the predicted gain logged first. It is never auto-merged, and the evaluator (hidden tests, chains, taxonomy) is checksummed and read-only (the DGM objective-hacking lesson).
- L3 release gate = held-out lead margin over the best CURRENT competitor (D19), ≥3 reps, a noise-floor arm.

NOVELTY claims, provisional (no counterexample found): zero-inference self-tuning where each adaptation is an auditable, reversible event; offline A/B of digest variants by replaying the append-only log; a memory product whose releases require pre-registered predictions and a sealed held-out chain.

RUN-OWNER QUESTION (2026-09-15): does sofar hurt small ad-hoc work ("quick bug fixes, random fixes") that still must be remembered? And does trimming bookkeeping hurt functionality?

Gap: chain A has only feature sessions, so round 1 never measures overhead on a 2-minute fix. The protocol's rule 2 ("work that matches no initiative requires `sofar new` first") makes a tiny fix pay the initiative ceremony: new, start, plan and write-back, several calls. So the overhead ratio is worst exactly there.

Proposals, awaiting approval:
(Q1) A QUICK-WORK LANE. Ad-hoc fixes land in a standing per-repo maintenance record, with no `sofar new` and no plan. Hooks capture files, commit, test result and error automatically (wave 2 W2.5). The agent adds ONE line of why only when it made a decision or rejected an approach. A fix that turns out bigger gets promoted to an initiative.
(Q2) Round 2 gets an ADDENDUM chain of short ad-hoc fix sessions (e.g. 5 bug-fix prompts of 1–3 minutes each), measuring:
- overhead ratio: sofar tokens and turns ÷ task tokens and turns
- whether each fix is later recalled (a probe session asks "why did X change")
It is frozen before round 2 like the main pre-registration; round 1 stays untouched (D5).

Trimming principle, the answer given:
- remove WASTE (duplicate starts, re-reading injected state, a second ToolSearch, constraint echoes, a second end_session);
- keep ESSENTIAL memory (decisions, why, rejected approaches, next action);
- MOVE mechanical facts (files, commits, tests) from model tool calls to automatic hooks, so capture goes up while tokens go down.
Every trim is gated in round 2 on C2/C3/C5 not dropping (D19 margin gate). A trim that loses recall is reverted.
